security_spec.violation_condition: OpenSBI M-mode code probes for 'Smaiae' as a distinct ISA extension string or device-tree property to gate AIA CSR access, save/restore, or initialization paths. After Smaiae removal, hardware reports Smaia directly, causing extension detection to miss, thereby skipping M-mode AIA CSR configuration (e.g., mvip, mvien writeability determination) that was previously conditioned on Smaiae presence.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: "smaiae" OR "Smaiae" OR "SMAIAE" in extension discovery, CSR capability probing, or conditional CSR access guards
affected_entities: extension detection / ISA string matching logic
security_spec.summary: Smaiae extension removed; OpenSBI must rewire all M-mode AIA CSR gating from Smaiae to Smaia detection, or interrupt controller init and context save/restore will be silently skipped

findings.finding: AIA detection uses CSR_MTOPI probe (SBI_HART_EXT_SMAIA), not ISA-string matching. The code never references 'Smaiae' as a distinct extension. After Smaiae removal, hardware reporting Smaia directly will still pass the CSR_MTOPI read-allowed check, so AIA CSR configuration (mvip, mvien, mstateen, etc.) is not gated on the Smaiae string. No missed detection possible.
mstateen0 AIA/IMSIC bits are gated on SBI_HART_EXT_SMAIA (CSR_MTOPI based), not on Smaiae string matching. No vulnerability window.

FDT ISA string parsing iterates over sbi_hart_ext[] table, which registers 'smaia' (not 'smaiae'). The string comparison matches against 'smaia', so hardware DT reporting 'smaia' will correctly set SBI_HART_EXT_SMAIA.
Extension name registered as 'smaia', matching the post-removal ISA naming. No 'smaiae' string present in the extension table.
